extracted.intended_audience: Wikipedia editors, members of WikiProject Mathematics, and MediaWiki developers concerned with mathematical typography
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluation criteria for how mathematical formulae should be authored, rendered, and presented on Wikipedia so they are legible, editable, and robust across browsers and user configurations. Covers rendering pipelines (texhtml/PNG/MathML), inline/display style conventions, accessibility, and desired tooling/enhancements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good typesetting (legible, correct, attractive)
rubrics_metrics.description: Math formulas should serve readers and editors and be displayed legibly, correctly, and attractively both on-screen and in print.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for readable, correct typography for displayed and inline mathematics. This is a high-level goal that guides decisions about rendering engines, font choices, spacing, and default math styles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Easy writing / easy to edit
rubrics_metrics.description: Formulas should be easy to write and edit for people from varied backgrounds — notably via TeX, HTML, and graphical equation editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tools and conventions should minimize verbosity and complexity for editors (e.g., avoid requiring manual \\textstyle for inline math). Provide or support multiple authoring paths (TeX, HTML, graphical editors) so novices and experts can both contribute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transformability and accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Math should be able to be transformed into other forms (e.g., read by screen-readers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep markup and rendering pipelines that permit conversion to MathML or other accessible forms. Avoid hacks that break semantic structure so that assistive technologies can interpret formulas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Considerations for developers (maintainability/fallbacks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematical typesetting software can be difficult to write and maintain; typography should 'just work' but accommodations should be made if something is difficult to implement in software.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When proposing changes, balance ideal typographic behavior with implementation cost and maintenance burden. Prefer solutions that are robust and maintainable across MediaWiki deployments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistent rendering across texhtml and PNG (sizing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure consistent display in both TeX-to-PNG and TeX-to-HTML rendering; the sizing of texhtml and PNGs should be consistent with HTML text and with each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid situations where texhtml is too big for some users while PNG is too large or too small for others. Do not rely on per-formula hacks to correct sizing; fix the rendering pipeline so output has consistent, legible size relative to surrounding text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inline math default style (textstyle vs displaystyle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inline equations should be set in \textstyle while displayed equations should be set in \displaystyle; by default all equations are set in \displaystyle leading to verbosity when correcting inline math.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer changing conventions so math mode defaults to textstyle for inline use (e.g., new tag like <mathtx> or change convention so <math> denotes displaystyle). Provide shorter ways to set textstyle so authors do not have to write \textstyle{...} for inline formulas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid using \scriptstyle as a hack
rubrics_metrics.description: \scriptstyle should never be necessary; it is used as a hack to produce smaller PNG output but creates problems (too small on some displays, verbose, breaks spacing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use \scriptstyle to adjust PNG sizes. Instead, fix PNG rendering size or use proper style conventions so spacing and scripts render correctly. Treat \scriptstyle usage as an anti-pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: PNG baseline alignment for inline formulas
rubrics_metrics.description: The baseline on inline PNG images is often too low or too high, resulting in the PNG not flowing with the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure inline PNGs have correct baseline alignment so subscripts/superscripts and simple sub-/super-script-only expressions align with surrounding text. This is difficult but important for inline flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linebreaks between </math> and trailing punctuation
rubrics_metrics.description: Linebreaks may be inserted between </math> and trailing punctuation, producing awkward breaks (e.g., math expression followed by a period on its own line).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Possible fixes include including punctuation within math mode (may render ugly) or using {{nowrap}}; ideally rendering should avoid requiring such workarounds so punctuation does not separate from math.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inline line spacing with formulas
rubrics_metrics.description: Line spacing needs to accommodate inline formula height so lines are not too tall or overlapping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure CSS and rendering rules adjust line-height appropriately for inline formulas to maintain readable vertical rhythm; test across fonts and user preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serif vs. sans-serif font mismatch
rubrics_metrics.description: PNG rendering defaults to serif fonts while many skins use sans-serif fonts, creating typographic clash.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Align math image font choices with site skin fonts or adopt web-fonts/HTML-based rendering to avoid mismatch. Consider user-configurable math font settings or use texhtml/MathML that matches page font.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robustness across browsers, OSes, and user configurations
rubrics_metrics.description: Rendering is limited by different web browsers, operating systems, and fonts in the browser; rendering must be tested and made robust across configurations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating rendering, account for browser/OS/font variability and wiki preferences (My preferences → Appearance → Skin/Math). Test on a fresh account/public computer to see default rendering. Prefer solutions that degrade gracefully across environments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness of rendering infrastructure and dependencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Know the rendering pipeline: pure HTML rendering, texhtml CSS style, TeX rendering using texvc for PNG (historical), and MathML output. Rendering depends on wiki configuration and extensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document and prefer rendering paths that are maintainable; when proposing changes, consider which engines (texvc, MathJax, Blahtex, MathML) are in use and their compatibility with existing LaTeX on pages. Use resources like Wikipedia:Rendering math and MediaWiki config pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desire for tooling/enhancements (formula editor, commutative diagrams)
rubrics_metrics.description: Long-term enhancements desirable: a formula editor to ease novice authoring, easier creation of commutative diagrams (including Xy-pic support), and graphical editors for simple equations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize development of authoring tools that reduce entry barriers for editors and reduce need for manual markup hacks. Recognize such features may require significant development work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing best-practice (test on fresh/default configuration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Safest way to test default rendering is to view a page while not logged in, on a fresh install or public computer, rather than on your own account & browser.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating how math displays to average users, test with default preferences and different skins to catch sizing/alignment issues that an individual editor's local setup might hide.
